  "summary": "S1 [fact] The target is the existing dependency-free Node.js help-desk service, with its documented HTTP startup, PORT configuration and bin/ CLI; discovery must verify those repository details. S2 [fact] The outcome is bulk ticket import for migration from the old tracker, usable through the service API; no broader migration tooling is requested. S3 [fact] POST /tickets/import accepts the specified tickets array with at most 5000 existing-format items, processes them in order and rejects an invalid item atomically with a 400 error naming its zero-based index. S4 [fact] A successful import returns 201 with the created count and new IDs in input order. S5 [fact] Every imported ticket receives the same recording and requester-notification behavior as a single creation; operational-failure guarantees require discovery. S6 [fact] A 5000-ticket import must receive its answer within ten seconds; the measurement environment must be recorded. S7 [fact] Existing service behavior and unchanged existing tests must continue to pass. S8 [fact] New behavior needs node:test coverage under test/, included in npm test. [Assumption] Discovery inspects README.md, src/server.js, bin/, test/, package metadata and the existing creation, storage and notification paths; these are source leads, not independently verified evidence. No team, channel, internal site, private repository or owner was named, and 'old tracker' identifies migration context without specifying a source integration. [Assumption] Import callers use the existing API identity and visibility model; discovery must establish actors, identification, shared state, lifetime, termination, hidden data and runtime-provided behavior. This default rules out adding identity, sharing or retention features without evidence. [Boundary] This unattended intake implements nothing and authorizes work only in the existing service; a person-only decision remains open if discovery finds that operational-failure guarantees cannot be inferred. [Delivery] The outcome is visible to API consumers in the returned source checkout after implementation and final return; an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until that return. No deployed target was named, and deployed behavior would exist only after release."
